deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is the continuation of an administrative expert report (Gutachten) addressed to the Hannoverian government through the Göttingen University Curatorium. In the second hand of the next page the report refers to 'Professor Riemann' in the third person, so the text was probably drafted for or about Riemann; who wrote it is not settled here. The subject is Hannover's possible participation in the Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung) proposed by Prussia under General-Lieutenant J. J. Baeyer around 1861–62.

Content of the page:
(a) It ends the argument begun on the previous page. Deriving the figure of the Earth from (1) connected triangulations, (2) refined astronomical latitude and longitude determinations and (3) systematic gravity determinations is an indivisible, purely scientific task. It needs full freedom and cannot be directed by binding rules. Therefore the most important thing the Hannoverian government can do is to publish the results of the Hannoverian arc measurement (Gauss's triangulation of the 1820s) completely and in detail, so that anyone can work on them further. A clause, 'der die dazu erforderlichen Fähigkeiten besitzt' ('who has the necessary abilities'), is struck through.
(b) It summarises the recommended points:
- Point 1: connect the Göttingen observatory by telegraph to the Göttingen telegraph station, and entrust the telegraphic determination of longitude differences between Göttingen and other telegraph-connected observatories to Observator Dr. Klinkerfues.
- Point 2: entrust the publication of the Hannoverian arc-measurement results to a suitable person. The text continues on the next page: if that person is found in Hannover, he should cooperate with Professor Schering to use Gauss's manuscript Nachlass; if the work is done in Göttingen, the Hannover files should be sent there.
- Point 3 (next page): authorise Professor Riemann to confer with Baeyer, without any obligation to direct or take part in the work.
(c) Pencil marginalia, apparently by a later editor or reviser, rephrase point 2 as a request to the 'Hohes Curatorium' ('High Curatorium') to arrange that a suitable person be encouraged and enabled to edit the Hannoverian Gradmessung.
(d) A footnote cites Gauss, 'Bestimmung des Breitenunterschiedes zwischen den Sternwarten von Göttingen und Altona' (1828), where only the astronomical observations were published. It then quotes Art. 20, p. 73 of that work. In the quoted passage Gauss foresees that later centuries will greatly advance knowledge of the Earth's figure, especially once national triangulations are linked into one large system. The quotation continues on the next page with the European observatory network.

No mathematical problem is posed or solved.

results.what: Recommendation that Gauss's Hannoverian arc-measurement (triangulation) results be fully published and that Göttingen take part in telegraphic longitude determinations, as Göttingen/Hannover's contribution to Baeyer's Central European arc measurement
results.modern_name: History of geodesy: the origins of the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (1862), later the Internationale Erdmessung
results.usually_credited_to: J. J. Baeyer (initiative, 1861); Gauss (Hannoverian Gradmessung, 1821–1825; quoted vision of linked European triangulations, 1828)

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely administrative and scientific-policy text with no mathematics. It is a minor documentary detail of Riemann's (or his Göttingen colleagues') involvement in the 1862 Gradmessung consultation. That episode is known in outline, so the page offers no new mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: Line 7: the clause 'der die dazu erforderlichen Fähigkeiten besitzt,' is indeed struck through in the image, so the marking is correct.
Line 3: 'nach unserem Ermessen' is consistent with the image; the [?] can probably be dropped.
The pencil insertion below the last line is faint. It reads roughly 'würde ganz ... sein'. 'besonders' is uncertain and the reading should stay marked as doubtful.

The footnote's cited work is Gauss, 'Bestimmung des Breitenunterschiedes zwischen den Sternwarten von Göttingen und Altona durch Beobachtungen am Ramsdenschen Zenithsector' (1828). The quotation is from Art. 20 of that work.

In the quotation, 'Vervielfältigung' runs off the edge of the page, and the final word of the last line ('verbinden'?) is cut off by the torn margin. Gauss's original wording should be checked; 'vereinigen' or a similar verb is possible.
Left-margin pencil, first lines: 'wodurch der Antrag gerechtfertigt erscheinen dürfte' fits the image.
